programme: TP53 stabilized by its Tudor-domain partner PHF20, driving the CDKN1A(p21)/CDKN2A(p16)-mediated cell-cycle-arrest and apoptotic stress-response arm of the p53 pathway
role_in_a: In COVID-19, cytopathic viral replication imposes genotoxic/proteotoxic stress that engages p53-dependent arrest/apoptosis and interferon crosstalk; the record only carries an Open Targets association score for TP53 in COVID-19 (0.8444 percentile), with no retrieved paper placing it there directly.
role_in_b: In Liver_Cancer, TP53 is the canonical tumor suppressor whose loss or dysregulation permits hepatocyte transformation; this is directly documented here by four retrieved papers on TP53 in liver/HCC contexts and by ReMap ChIP-seq binding at 7 of its 25 listed targets, consistent with an actively engaged regulatory node rather than a passive association.
shared_axis: A cytopathic viral infection and a hepatic tumor both generate persistent cellular stress (replicative, genotoxic, or proteotoxic) that funnels through the p53 checkpoint; PHF20's role in binding methylated p53 and blocking its MDM2-mediated turnover would be the shared molecular dial setting whether stressed cells arrest, senesce, or die in both tissues.
reasoning: TP53 is independently and concretely documented in liver cancer in this record (four papers plus ReMap binding), giving one half of the module real footing, but its COVID-19 evidence is only an association percentile with no supporting paper, and PHF20 has zero disease-specific evidence on either side. The pairing rests on a real, specific molecular complex (p53 stabilized by PHF20) rather than a vague 'immune response' label, which keeps it above incoherent, but the cross-disease connection itself is reasoned from general p53 biology rather than retrieved literature.
support: PMID 39519042 (TP53/CHEK2 variants in a pediatric liver tumor), PMID 41097767 (TP53 associated with a non-cirrhotic hepatic condition), PMID 38276007 (network pharmacology study implicating TP53 in a hepatic disease model), PMID 28962365 (TP53-linked CDKN1B/CDKN1C dysregulation in hepatocellular carcinoma-derived cells). None found for PHF20 in either disease; none found for TP53 specifically in COVID-19 beyond the association score.
how_to_falsify: In SARS-CoV-2-infected hepatocyte or airway epithelial lines and in TP53-mutant versus TP53-wildtype HCC lines, knock down PHF20 and measure p53 protein half-life (cycloheximide chase or western blot) and induction of CDKN1A/CDKN2A; if PHF20 loss does not destabilize p53 or blunt p21/p16 induction in either context, or if PHF20 and TP53 signal do not co-vary across the patient groups where both were jointly supported, the proposed module is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (COVID cohorts) versus liver (HCC cohorts), drawn from 40 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs. TP53 itself has the lowest recurrence (28/40) of the concordant set, so the anchor factor is not the top-ranked one. The single-view exclusions (NFATC3, TBX6) and the tissue-generic exclusions (ZBTB4, IKZF1, HLX, JUNB, CREB5, SMAD3, BRCA1, GFI1, IRF1, ETS2, SPI1, EBF1) remove several plausible 'master immune/liver regulator' alternatives — their absence here is by design, not a gap to fill in. Several other concordant factors (NFIA, IKZF2, FOSL1, DOT1L) carry COVID-specific literature support but no liver-cancer evidence in this record and were deliberately left out of the module rather than folded in, since nothing here ties them mechanistically to the TP53/PHF20 axis.
